content:
Doc purpose
- Capture what worked / didn’t work in the TP stability initiative (multi-GPU TP hangs/timeouts under load).
- Identify tooling/process gaps that created drag.
- List follow-up actions (some are not in ENG-2401 umbrella; this doc is the “parking lot” that should become tickets).

Meeting
- Date: 2025-03-27 (retro session #1)
- Facilitator: Talia Benson
- Notes: rough / draft; please add corrections inline

Attendees (partial)
- Runtime scheduling: Sofia Ivanova, Marcus Reed, Julian Moore
- Kernels/collectives: Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato
- Observability: Omar El-Sayed, Allison Grant (joined late)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Tomáš Novák
- Release/CI: Connor O'Brien, Sahana Iyer
- Support liaison: Dev Patel

Project recap (what we shipped)
- Scheduler:
  - TP-group health model + state machine; stop scheduling onto quarantined groups (PR 18432)
  - Cancellation path hardening to prevent barrier deadlocks (PR 18441)
- Collectives:
  - Periodic async error checks + clearer failure propagation to scheduler (PR 18455)
  - Collective timeout tuning knobs + deployment-mode defaults (PR 18473)
- Watchdog:
  - Per-TP-group forward progress watchdog; quarantine + controlled teardown (PR 18462)
- Observability:
  - Structured logs around collective stalls / scheduler starvation; trace/span annotations (PR 18470)
  - Dashboard + alerts in observability pack (PR 502)
- Testing:
  - Deterministic-ish stress runner with fault injection, wired into CI/perf-canary (PR 18480 + perf-canary PR 288)

Primary goal (from kickoff)
- Eliminate “stuck TP group” class of incidents where a TP worker group stops making forward progress (hanging streams, request timeouts/5xx under sustained load).

Success criteria (how we measured it during rollout)
- Reduction in:
  - TP-related request timeouts (client-visible)
  - “stream never completes” cases (server-side streaming sessions > N minutes with no tokens)
  - oncall pages attributed to TP hangs / NCCL stalls
- Increase in:
  - time-to-diagnosis (TTD) for TP hang signatures (comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation)
  - automatic recovery rate via quarantine/teardown (vs manual pool drain)

Observed outcomes (qualitative; numbers live in dashboards)
- Canary pools: watchdog/quarantine helped break “infinite hang” loops; we saw several stuck groups self-quarantine and recover without draining the whole host pool.
- Dedicated: opt-in customers reported fewer “permanent” stalls; still seeing performance variability when networks are marginal (out-of-scope but impacts perceived stability).
- Oncall: improved ability to answer “is this comm stall or kernel stall?” quickly due to structured logs + progress counters. Still too much manual spelunking for some cases (see gaps).

What went well
1) We got a real repro harness earlier than usual
- The stress/fault-injection runner changed the dynamic: we stopped arguing about “is it real” and started iterating.
- The ability to force rank delay + forced cancel was directly useful in validating barrier/cancel fixes.
- Having perf-canary run nightly created a forcing function to keep scenarios stable.

2) Clear failure-domain boundary: TP-group quarantine
- We aligned on “TP group is the failure domain” for most hangs; not host-wide drains by default.
- Scheduler refusing to enqueue work onto quarantined groups was a big reliability win (and reduced cascading effects).

3) Feature flags + rollout hygiene
- Config knobs for watchdog sensitivity and collective timeouts made staged rollout possible.
- Release coordination thread was tight; we had explicit rollback triggers and a clear owner.

4) Cross-functional cadence (SRE + Runtime)
- Weekly check-ins with SRE produced better alert thresholds and fewer surprise pages.
- Having SRE define operational ownership early prevented “who owns the pager for this metric?” confusion (not perfect, but better than prior efforts).

What didn’t go well / pain points
1) We were late on “minimum viable observability”
- We built significant instrumentation mid-stream (ENG-2404), but during the first 1–2 weeks we were flying blind.
- We still lack a single “TP group health” panel that unifies: collective lat + progress + queueing + cancellations + watchdog state in one place. We have pieces.

2) Cancellation semantics were under-specified
- Multiple code paths “cancel” a request (client disconnect, server deadline, upstream circuit breaker). Not all paths were equivalent.
- Barrier + cancellation interplay was discovered via production symptom, not via design. We need a written contract: what can be canceled, when, and what cleanup must happen on each rank.

3) Watchdog tuning had avoidable churn
- First pass had false positives under legitimate long-prefill workloads (mixed seq lengths).
- We improved defaults later, but we burned time arguing about whether it was a bug or “expected slowness.”
- We need a clearer definition: “stuck” vs “slow,” and which signals qualify as forward progress.

4) Ownership boundaries: scheduler vs collectives
- Some bugs were “shared responsibility” (e.g., async error surfaces in collective layer but scheduler must react correctly). This caused a couple of multi-day delays waiting for the “right” person.
- Suggestion: for future cross-layer reliability work, assign a single DRI per failure mode (not per subsystem).

5) Customer comms vs engineering reality
- Support/CS had to answer “when will a fix be out?” while we were still determining root causes.
- We did okay after week ~3, but earlier comms were fuzzy (status updates too technical or too hedged).

6) CI signal quality
- Early versions of the stress test were flaky (timing-sensitive) and resulted in some “red CI” fatigue.
- We reduced flake by adding pass/fail thresholds and better artifact capture, but we need to treat this harness like a product (versioned scenarios, clear baselines).

Surprises / things we learned
- “No forward progress” is not always NCCL.
  - Some hangs were scheduler starvation patterns: one rank lagging + barrier wait + cancellation path leaving state inconsistent.
- Mixed sequence lengths are a stability amplifier.
  - Long-prefill + short-decode mixes increased risk of watchdog false positives and exposed fairness issues.
- Partial failure modes are more common than we assumed.
  - One rank going slow or dropping out temporarily is enough to poison a whole group if errors don’t surface quickly.

Decisions we made (and would keep)
- Keep quarantine as first response; avoid whole-host drains unless we see correlated host-level issues.
- Treat async error checks as mandatory in TP mode (with a controlled overhead budget).
- Prefer “explicit abort policy” over silent stalls; correctness + recovery beats hanging.

Things we would do differently next time
- Start with an “observability pack stub” in week 1 (even if ugly):
  - per-rank progress counter
  - collective latency histogram
  - watchdog state + reason codes
  - cancellation counts by cause
- Define the cancellation contract in writing before touching code.
- Run a structured “failure mode review” up front (30–60 min) with one DRI per failure mode.
- For stress harnesses: require artifact capture (rank traces, last N log lines, watchdog snapshot) as a first-class output.

Tooling / platform gaps (still painful)
- Rank-level trace capture is too manual.
  - We need a one-click “collect TP group dump” equivalent: last known progress, last collective op, queue depth, cancellation map, watchdog state.
- NCCL/kernel attribution still requires expertise.
  - We need better automatic classification: comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation (even if only 70% accurate).
- No standardized “reason codes” across layers.
  - Watchdog triggers, scheduler timeouts, and collective timeouts emit different strings; hard to aggregate.
- Dedicated environments are variable.
  - We need a documented compatibility matrix (driver/NCCL versions we test) surfaced to Support/CS and field teams.

Follow-ups / action items (convert to tickets)
P0 (next 2–3 weeks)
- Define and document cancellation contract for TP execution (what’s allowed, required cleanup, invariants).
  - Owner: Sofia Ivanova + Noah Patel
  - Output: short spec + code pointers + tests to lock behavior
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2561
- Add unified TP-group health panel (single-pane view) + link from oncall runbook.
  - Owner: Omar El-Sayed + Sergio Costa
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2562
- Standardize “reason codes” for TP group transitions + watchdog triggers (enum + structured log field).
  - Owner: Julian Moore
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2563

P1 (this quarter)
- Build “tp-group dump” command/tool (runtime endpoint + SRE automation) that snapshots state for a single group.
  - Owner: Jacob Stein + Rafael Mendes
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2570
- Improve automatic classification of stall type using existing signals (heuristics first).
  - Owner: Allison Grant + Omar El-Sayed
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2571
- Extend stress harness scenario coverage:
  - mixed seq length fairness + long-prefill patterns
  - intermittent rank delay (not just fixed delay)
  - forced cancel storm
  - Owner: Sahana Iyer + Marcus Reed
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2572
- Dedicated compatibility guidance doc (driver/NCCL/runtime versions + what we validate) for Support/CS.
  - Owner: Kira Thompson + Dev Patel
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2573

P2 (nice-to-have / dependent)
- Evaluate whether we want per-request “collective budget” accounting (detect pathological requests early; shed load before poisoning group).
  - Owner: Lena Fischer
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2580
- Explore adding a lightweight “heartbeat kernel” or device-side progress marker to distinguish kernel stalls more reliably.
  - Owner: Hiro Tanaka + Grace Kim
  - Suggested ticket: ENG-2581

Open questions / parking lot
- Should quarantine ever be “sticky” (i.e., permanently remove a TP group from rotation until host restart), or always attempt controlled teardown + rejoin?
- For Dedicated: do we default-enable watchdog/quarantine in the next minor, or keep opt-in longer? (PM decision + customer trust tradeoff.)
- Do we need different watchdog thresholds for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints, or can we unify with better progress signals?

Notes to self (Talia)
- Ensure action items are reflected in ENG-2401 umbrella or a follow-on umbrella (ENG-25xx). This retro doc should not become the system of record.
- Ask Support/CS: was comms good enough? What was missing in week 1–2?
- Ask SRE: are alerts now actionable, or still noisy?
